description:
Hi, I'm Nikhil, a first-year BTech CSE student who loves space and learns by building.

Space science has fascinated me for a long time, and I've turned that interest into real experience. I've competed in IAAC twice, reaching the finals both times and earning a gold certificate. I've also taken part in NASA's citizen scientist asteroid-finder programs, where I helped search real telescope data for asteroids.
summary:
Noble Spectra is an interactive explorer for SPHEREx infrared observations. It lets users inspect real archive images across observation epochs, rank possible moving-source tracks with a machine-learning model, and review exploratory motion fits and wavelength–time traces.

The model learns from simulated sources injected into real image backgrounds using empirical point-spread functions. It ranks candidate paths for human review; it does not claim to detect or identify a planet. By making changes between observations easier to inspect, Noble Spectra supports the search for faint moving objects that may be missed in individual images. The project addresses the challenge by turning SPHEREx time-series data into an approachable, evidence-focused investigation tool, while clearly distinguishing archive observations from simulated examples and showing the limits of short-baseline measurements.
details:
Noble Spectra turns SPHEREx’s infrared observations into a hands-on hunt for objects that move between the frames. Users can load real archive images, blink through epochs, and explore the changing sky. An injection-trained machine-learning model ranks possible motion paths, marked with translucent red dots, so intriguing candidates rise to the top for human review. Each candidate can also be explored with an experimental WCS-based motion fit and a wavelength–time trace built from SPHEREx’s wavelength metadata and measured image brightness.

The project’s ambition is to make time-domain astronomy feel tangible: help people spot patterns across repeated observations and investigate faint, fast-moving objects that a single image might hide. It brings data exploration, machine learning, and visual storytelling together in one polished observatory-style interface.

Noble Spectra is built with React, JavaScript, and Vite on the frontend, and Python, FastAPI, Astropy, NumPy, and scikit-learn on the backend. It uses SPHEREx FITS data and empirical point-spread functions from NASA/IPAC IRSA. Scientific caution is built into the experience: candidate scores are rankings, injected sources are simulated, wavelength traces are sparse rather than full spectra, and short observation baselines cannot confirm proper motion. The goal is bold exploration—with the evidence and its limits visible at every step.
